question: How many countries will vote in favor of the IAEA resolution "Application of IAEA Safeguards in the Middle East" at the 70th General Conference?

calls.reasoning: The tally is a turnout statistic, not a contested political vote: 'against' has been 0 for years and abstentions sit at 7-9 (Israel, US, a few others), so the number is essentially how many delegations are in the room at the closing plenary. Reference class = the same resolution's annual roll-call, 2022-2025: 117, 115, 112, 120 (mean 116, SD 3.4), against a slow multi-decade upward drift (103 in 2009) tracking IAEA membership growth. I center slightly above the 4-year mean at 118: 2025's 120 was the recent high with record 127 votes cast, Middle East nuclear salience remains elevated into 2026 (Iran safeguards crisis, post-strike verification disputes), and the 70th-anniversary session plausibly draws strong attendance - but mean reversion from a high argues against simply anchoring on 120. Evidence is thin on 2026-specific signals (no GC70 draft text or attendance data found, and direct document fetches were blocked with HTTP 402, so historical tallies come via search extraction), so I stay close to the reference class. No prediction market prices this: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, or bookmakers, so there is no anchor to blend. Escape mass is small and asymmetric: falling below 100 needs a ~20-vote turnout collapse never observed in this era (1%); exceeding 130 needs record attendance plus current abstainers flipping (1.5%). Separately, ~3-5% annulment risk if the item is taken by consensus, which does not affect the conditional distribution.

SUBJECT: number of Member States recorded voting 'in favour' of the IAEA GC resolution 'Application of IAEA Safeguards in the Middle East', as a whole, at GC70 (2026).

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the roll-call 'in favour' count recorded in the resolution document itself (GC(70)/RES/nn) or the GC(70) compilation 'Resolutions adopted and other decisions taken during the seventieth regular session', published on the IAEA GC70 resolutions page. It resolves off the vote on the ENTIRE resolution, NOT the separate vote routinely held on operative paragraph 2, and NOT the total votes cast. Annulled if adopted by consensus/without a vote, or if no 'in favour' tally is recorded.

EVENT WINDOW: 14 Sept 2026 -> 18 Sept 2026 per the criteria (70th regular session; closing plenary Friday 18 Sept, when this item is customarily taken). As of Now = 2026-09-07T15:20Z, 0% elapsed; the session has not convened.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the resolution is tabled by Egypt, put to a recorded roll-call in the late-week plenary, and adopted with a tally in the same band as recent years.

EVIDENCE (source; date):
- 2025, GC(69)/RES/15: 120 in favour, 0 against, 7 abstentions. Total votes cast 127. (GC69 resolutions/compilation, IAEA; Sept 2025)
- 2024, GC(68)/RES/14: 112 in favour, 0 against, 9 abstentions. Total cast 121. Corroborated independently by Egypt Today reporting on Egypt's draft. (IAEA gc68-res14; Egypt Today; Sept 2024)
- 2023, GC(67)/RES/13: 115 in favour, 0 against, 8 abstentions; roll-call taken 28 September 2023. Total cast 123. (IAEA gc67-res13; Sept 2023)
- 2022, GC(66)/RES/12: 117 in favour, 0 against, 7 abstentions. Total cast 124. (IAEA gc66 resolutions; Sept 2022)
- 2009: 103 in favour, 0 against, 4 abstentions, adopted 17 September 2009. (IAEA GC record; Sept 2009)
- The separate operative-paragraph-2 vote runs a different tally and has drawn 1 against in several years: 2019 OP2 117-1-10; 2022 OP2 115-1-9; 2024 OP2 112-1-7. (IAEA resolution documents)
- 'Against' on the resolution as a whole has been 0 in every recent year; abstentions have ranged 7-9. Israel places on record deep concerns about a 'non-consensual and politically motivated' text; the US criticises politicisation of the agenda item; Iran abstained in 2025 citing the text's handling of the prior conference outcome. (IAEA GC69 records; US Mission Vienna statement, Agenda Item 20, Sept 2025)
- GC70 runs 14-18 September 2026 at the Vienna International Centre; it is the 70th consecutive annual session and is being framed as a milestone/anniversary session. (IAEA GC70 page; IAEA 'The Year Ahead: Key Events at the IAEA in 2026')
- GC(69)/RES/15 requested the Director General to report on implementation and to re-place the item on the GC70 provisional agenda; the question text places it at agenda item 19. (GC69 resolution text)
- IAEA rules: each Member has one vote; a majority of Members constitutes a quorum in plenary; decisions on such questions are by a majority of members present and voting. IAEA membership is roughly 180, so the tally reflects a subset of Members present and voting, well below full membership. (IAEA Rules of Procedure of the General Conference; IAEA Statute)
- Context carried into 2026: Iran safeguards remain in dispute at the Board of Governors, with a March 2026 Board resolution urging Iranian cooperation and DG reporting on the effect of regional conflict on safeguards and verification; ISIS published analysis of IAEA Iran verification reports in June 2026. (IAEA DG introductory statement, Board of Governors 2-6 March 2026; GOV/2026/8, 27 Feb 2026; ISIS report, June 2026)
- At GC69, Iran was reported to be preparing a separate draft resolution on attacks against peaceful nuclear facilities, indicating multiple competing Middle East-related texts can appear in the same session. (IRNA via GlobalSecurity.org; Sept 2025)

BASE RATES:
- Over all four most recent sessions (2022-2025), whole-resolution 'in favour': 117, 115, 112, 120; mean 116.0, SD 3.4, min 112, max 120. (IAEA resolution documents)
- Over the same four sessions, total votes cast (in favour + against + abstentions): 124, 123, 121, 127; mean 123.8. 'In favour' has been 93-95% of total votes cast each year. (derived from the same documents)
- Year-over-year change in 'in favour' over the three observed transitions 2022->2025: -2, -3, +8. (derived)
- Over the longer horizon 2009 -> 2025, 'in favour' rose from 103 to 120, roughly +1 per year, alongside growth in IAEA membership. (IAEA GC records)
- Conditional on the item being put to a recorded vote: in every observed recent session the resolution passed with 0 against. Conditional on prior-year tally being at the top of its recent range (2025 = 120, the four-year high), there is only one comparable transition in the modern record, so the conditional evidence for reversion vs continuation is weak.
- Rate of adoption by consensus (which would annul): 0 of the last 4 sessions, and none found in the modern record; the item has gone to roll-call annually for decades.

MARKETS: no prediction market on this quantity was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, or any bookmaker.

calls.reference_class: Annual recorded roll-call 'in favour' totals on the IAEA General Conference resolution 'Application of IAEA Safeguards in the Middle East' as a whole, 2009-2025 (with 2022-2025 weighted most heavily)

calls.reasoning: The tally is not really a contest over the text - 'against' has been 0 every recent year - it is a proxy for how many delegations are present at the Friday closing plenary and how many of the usual ~7-11 Western/Israeli abstainers show up. Total ballots cast ran 121-128 over 2018-2025, with 'in favour' 112-120. Base rate from that class is ~117; last year printed 120 (127 voting), the top of the range, immediately after the June 2025 strikes on Iran. 2026 has an even larger version of the same shock (Feb 2026 US/Israeli strikes, Iranian attacks on Gulf states, UNSC 2817, a June 2026 Board non-compliance resolution), which argues for high salience and high attendance, plus one more member state (181 since Dec 2025). Against that: mean reversion off a high print, an Arab-Iranian rupture that could cool Arab Group energy for the regional-nuclear file, and the possibility of a hardened text (attacks on nuclear facilities) that pushes a few habitual yes votes into abstention. I center slightly above the multi-year mean but below 2025, with a fatter left tail because a thin Friday plenary is the single most common way this number falls (2024's 112). Escape mass is small in both directions: >130 in favour would need ~138 ballots cast, far above anything in a decade; <100 would need ~15-20 defections or absences versus 2025 - only a walkout, boycott, or heavily contested rewrite gets there. Evidence on the 2026 text itself is thin: I could not find GC(70)/1, the draft, or any GC70 reporting, so I stay close to the reference class. No prediction market prices this (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold: none found), so no crowd anchor.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the recorded roll-call tally of Member States voting 'in favour' on the resolution AS A WHOLE at GC70 - not the separate vote on operative paragraph 2, which is tallied differently every year, and not the number of co-sponsors. Tally is printed in a footnote of the resolution document itself (GC(70)/RES/xx) and in the GC(70)/RES/DEC compilation.

EVENT WINDOW: 14 -> 18 September 2026 per the criteria (70th regular session, Vienna International Centre); the vote historically falls in the closing plenary on the final day. As of Now (2026-09-07T15:20Z) the window has not opened - 0% elapsed, opens in ~6.4 days. Scheduled question resolution 2026-09-18.

RECORDED TALLIES FOR THIS SAME RESOLUTION (in favour / against / abstain; source: IAEA GC resolution documents and RES/DEC compilations):
- 2018 GC(62)/RES/12: 117 / 0 / 11 (128 ballots cast)
- 2019 GC(63)/RES/13: whole-resolution figure not retrieved; the separate vote on operative paragraph 2 was 117 / 1 / 10 (128 ballots cast)
- 2020 GC(64)/RES/15 and 2021 GC(65)/RES/14: adopted, tallies searched for but NOT FOUND in accessible sources. 2020 was a COVID-restricted session with reduced delegations.
- 2022 GC(66)/RES/12: 117 / 0 / 7 (124 cast)
- 2023 GC(67)/RES/13: 115 / 0 / 8 (123 cast) - roll-call taken at Egypt's request
- 2024 GC(68)/RES/14: 112 / 0 / 9 (121 cast); OP2 separately 112 / 1 / 7
- 2025 GC(69)/RES/15: 120 / 0 / 7 (127 cast)
Class note: these are UNCONDITIONAL over all recent sessions. Conditional on the prior year having had a major regional military event (2025, after the June 2025 strikes), the one available observation is the highest of the series.

MECHANICS: 'against' has been 0 in every recorded year found; the abstainer bloc (Israel, US, and a handful of other Western/Pacific states) has run 7-11. So 'in favour' ~= ballots cast minus ~7-9, and the dominant driver is attendance at the Friday closing plenary rather than any shift of position. Ballots cast ranged 121-128 across 2018-2025.

DENOMINATOR: IAEA membership is 181 as of Dec 2025 (Maldives deposited 4 Dec 2025), up from ~171 in 2018. Article XIX arrears suspensions remove a small number of voting rights each year (exact GC70 count not retrieved).

SAME-SESSION COMPARATORS (2025, showing attendance varies by item within one week): GC(69)/RES/14 (Ukraine) 62 / 7 / 46 = 115 cast; another GC69 resolution 96 / 5 / 17 = 118 cast; the Middle East safeguards item drew 127 cast.

2026 REGIONAL CONTEXT: US and Israel struck Iran on 28 Feb 2026, killing Supreme Leader Khamenei and hitting nuclear and military infrastructure; Iran attacked Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan. UNSC resolution 2817 (11 Mar 2026) condemned Iran's attacks, 13-0-2 (China and Russia abstaining), tabled by Bahrain for the GCC and Jordan, co-sponsored by 135 UN member states; a competing Russian draft failed. A Pakistan-mediated ceasefire and a June MOU halted large-scale fighting, with subsequent reciprocal strikes over alleged violations. (Sources: press.un.org sc16315, UN News 2026/03, globalsecurity.org)

IAEA-IRAN TRACK 2026: Iran suspended cooperation after the 2025 attacks, then readmitted inspectors; the Agency resumed some in-field work (routine inspection at Bushehr). Grossi told the Board on 8 June 2026 it had been almost a year since access to facilities damaged in the June 2025 attacks. On 10 June 2026 the Board adopted an E3+US resolution finding Iran's failure to address safeguards concerns outstanding over six years to constitute non-compliance with its CSA. IAEA has reported sharp degradation of nuclear safety and security in Iran from attacks on nuclear sites. (Sources: iaea.org Board news, gov.uk June 2026 statement)

ADJACENT AGENDA ITEM: 'Israeli Nuclear Capabilities' is a separate long-running item (agenda item 20 in 2025). The Arab Group chose NOT to introduce a resolution under it in 2025. Whether it introduces one in 2026 is unknown; a contested INC vote in the same plenary could change who is in the room for the Middle East safeguards vote in either direction. The 2013 INC resolution was defeated on the floor - precedent that a hardened Arab Group text can lose Western and swing-state support.

SPONSORSHIP / PROCEDURE: Egypt sponsors, coordinated through the League of Arab States. The 2025 text asked the DG to report on implementation and to place the item on the GC70 provisional agenda, where it is expected as agenda item 19. Israel has publicly objected to the text as 'non-consensual and politically motivated'.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: the GC(70)/1 provisional agenda or any GC70 document list; any 2026 draft text or reporting on whether the text has been amended (e.g. to address attacks on nuclear facilities); any statement of intent by any delegation on how it will vote in 2026; the 2020 and 2021 tallies; the 2019 whole-resolution tally; any indication that the item might be taken by consensus rather than roll-call in 2026 (relevant because the criteria annul the question in that case); the GC70 Article XIX arrears list. No prediction market on Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold prices this event - checked, none found.

STATUS QUO: the item is on the agenda, a roll-call is requested by Egypt, the resolution passes with zero against, and the 'in favour' count lands in the band this series has occupied for the last eight sessions.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the eight most recent recorded roll-call tallies on this same annually-repeated Egypt-sponsored resolution (2018-2025), whose median in-favour is 115 and whose full observed range is 111-120. The tally is turnout-driven, not preference-driven: zero votes against every year, abstentions a stable 7-13 Western/Israel-aligned bloc, so the number is essentially (delegations voting) minus (abstainers). Base rate 115; 2025 printed 120, the series max, and the series shows negative lag-1 autocorrelation (-0.31), so I shrink 120 back toward 115 rather than carrying it forward. Offsetting upward: membership rose to 181 (Maldives, Dec 2025), abstentions have trended down 13 -> 7 since 2018, the 70th-anniversary session should draw strong attendance, and Middle East nuclear salience remains high after the June 2026 Board resolution on Iran. Net median 117. Item is confirmed on the GC70 agenda (GC(70)/13 posted), so the annulment branch (adoption by consensus) is a live but small risk that does not shift the conditional distribution. No prediction market prices this. Escape mass is thin: sub-100 needs a turnout collapse ~13 below the COVID-year low, 131+ needs ~138 delegations voting versus an observed maximum of 128.

- The roll call on this item does not appear in GC(69)/OR.9 (the record containing the Ukraine roll call and the deferral of the attacks item), so the Middle East safeguards vote fell in a different plenary meeting of that session.

calls.reconciliation: Disputed: (a) the 2018 tally - Run 2 said 117/0/11, Run 3 said 115/0/13; both agree on 128 ballots cast, and 117/0/11 reconciles with the independently-corroborated 2019 OP2 line of 117/1/10 (also 128 cast), so I read 2018=115/0/13 and 2019=117/0/11 per Run 3, with Run 2 having shifted 2019 onto 2018. No web access this run, so this rests on internal consistency, not on the PDFs; impact on the median is under one vote either way. (b) Existence of 2020/2021 tallies - Runs 1 and 2 could not retrieve them, Run 3 reports 111 and 113; I accept Run 3 because it is the only run with working document retrieval this week (Run 1's fetches returned HTTP 402) and it independently surfaced live GC70 artifacts the others missed, but I down-weight those two years as a COVID attendance regime. (c) Reference-class window, 4 years vs 8 - judgment, resolved to the 8-year series with the COVID pair discounted, giving effective base ~116. (d) Whether 2025's 120 persists or reverts - pure judgment, no evidence breaks it; I take partial reversion because 120 was the series max at near-ceiling ballots cast and already reflected post-strike salience, so the 2026 shock is not a fresh increment. (e) Run 2's hardened-text/Arab-Iran-rupture defection story - unverifiable, no run found the 2026 draft, so it buys left-tail weight only. All three runs independently found no prediction market anywhere; I retrieved nothing myself this run.
